name: Washington
tagline: From Cape Flattery's sea cliffs to the Palouse hills, by ferry and Cascade pass.
intro: Washington's byways run the outer coast of the Olympic Peninsula and the islands of the Salish Sea by ferry, climb the Cascades by their passes, and cross the coulees, canyons and farm hills of the dry east side. This chapter follows the Washington State Scenic and Recreational Highway system, created by the Legislature in 1967 and run by the Washington State Department of Transportation, with the All-American Road around the Selkirks and the Forest Service's Mountain Loop listed separately. The law designates highway segments by route number, not byways by name, so the byway names and their roster come from local byway groups and State of Washington Tourism.

programs.label: Washington State Scenic and Recreational Highways (State Scenic Byways)

members.name: Cape Flattery Tribal Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Twelve miles across the Makah Reservation to the end of the road, past Neah Bay and the Makah Museum's Ozette artifacts, then a forest trail out to the sea cliffs facing Tatoosh Island.

members.name: Cascade Loop Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 440-mile ring over Stevens Pass, down the Columbia to Chelan, up the Methow and back across the North Cascades to the Skagit flats and a ferry from Whidbey Island. The high pass closes each winter.

members.name: Cascade Valleys Heritage Corridor
members.blurb: SR 202 leaves the Woodinville tasting rooms and follows the Snoqualmie River upstream, past the railway museum in Snoqualmie and the falls sacred to the Snoqualmie Tribe, to North Bend under Mount Si.

members.name: Chinook Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 410 climbs from the small town of Enumclaw through Federation Forest's old growth, skirts Mount Rainier's northeast flank and drops off Chinook Pass into the orchards of the Naches Valley. Closed in winter.

members.name: Chuckanut Drive
members.blurb: SR 11 crosses the Samish flats, where hawks hunt the winter fields, then winds along the shore of the Chuckanut Mountains past Larrabee State Park into Fairhaven. It opened in 1916 on an old logging route.

members.name: Columbia River Gorge Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 14 holds to the Columbia's north bank from Washougal, through wet forest past Stevenson and the windsurfing beaches at Bingen, into dry rolling hills and the concrete Stonehenge at Maryhill.

members.name: Coulee Corridor Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the sandhill-crane fields at Othello north through scabland lakes and Ice Age flood channels, past Dry Falls and the length of Banks Lake to Grand Coulee Dam and across the Colville Reservation to Omak.

members.name: Bay-2-Bay Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 105 links Grays Harbor to Willapa Bay, by the Westport lighthouse and fishing docks, past cranberry farms to the quiet marina at Tokeland, ending among Raymond's metal sculptures.
members.note: Shown on the map as Cranberry Coast Scenic Byway.

members.name: Hidden Coast Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 109 runs out of Hoquiam to the open Pacific and north along razor-clam beaches, past the old stumps of the Copalis ghost forest, to Taholah at the mouth of the Quinault River.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Lewis and Clark Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The long way down the Snake and Columbia, from Clarkston and the 1887 Dayton courthouse through Walla Walla's vineyards and the Tri-Cities to the gorge and the sea at Cape Disappointment.

members.name: Mount Baker Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 542 follows the Nooksack River out of Bellingham through the logging town of Deming and the forest past Nooksack Falls, climbing to Artist Point on a last stretch that stays closed from autumn into June.

members.name: Mountains to Sound Greenway
members.blurb: Interstate 90 as a forest road, leaving Lake Washington for the Issaquah Alps and the salmon hatchery, then climbing through the forested Cascades over Snoqualmie Pass and down to the end of the byway at Thorp.

members.name: North Cascades Scenic Highway
members.blurb: SR 20 leaves the Skagit at Concrete's old cement silos, passes the powerhouse at Newhalem and the green water of Diablo Lake, and crosses Washington Pass under Liberty Bell into the Methow. Closed in winter.

members.name: North Pend Oreille Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 31 starts at Tiger's lone 1913 store and follows the Pend Oreille north past Box Canyon Dam to the old mining town of Metaline Falls and the limestone passages of Gardner Cave near the border.

members.name: Okanogan Trails Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 97 follows the Okanogan River north from Pateros past the site of old Fort Okanogan, through the river towns of Okanogan and Omak and along the edge of the Colville Reservation to the border at Oroville.

members.name: Pacific Coast Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 101 runs the oyster shore of Hood Canal, the lavender fields at Sequim and Port Angeles, then turns down the rain-forest side of the Olympics to the coast and on south to the Columbia.

members.name: Palouse Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highways web the rolling farm hills of Whitman County around Steptoe Butte, Colfax and Pullman, past the Dahmen Barn's wagon-wheel fence at Uniontown, with a side road to Palouse Falls.

members.name: Pend Oreille Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 20 follows the Pend Oreille north from Newport, past old log-boom pilings left from the Cusick match mill and the Kalispel bison pastures across the river, to the crossroads at Tiger.

members.name: San Juan Islands Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A ferry from Anacortes threads the islands to Friday Harbor, then island roads to Roche Harbor's marina and, by a second boat, across Orcas Island to Eastsound and Moran State Park.

members.name: Sherman Pass Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Republic, where visitors dig for Eocene fossils, SR 20 climbs through larch and fir to Sherman Pass, the highest maintained pass in the state, and descends past an old log flume to Lake Roosevelt.

members.name: Spirit Lake Memorial Highway
members.blurb: SR 504 follows the North Fork Toutle from Castle Rock into the 1980 blast zone of Mount St. Helens, past Coldwater Lake, born of the avalanche, toward Johnston Ridge and its view into the crater.

members.name: Stevens Pass Greenway
members.blurb: US 2 climbs the Skykomish valley from Monroe past Gold Bar, Index and the long drop of Wallace Falls, crosses Stevens Pass and comes down the east side to the Bavarian storefronts of Leavenworth.

members.name: Strait of Juan de Fuca Highway
members.blurb: SR 112 winds west from Port Angeles along the Strait, by the Joyce general store and the tidepools at Salt Creek, through the fishing villages of Sekiu and Clallam Bay to Neah Bay on the Makah Reservation.

members.name: Swiftwater Corridor Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Back roads from the Salmon La Sac campground at the edge of the Alpine Lakes Wilderness, through the old coal town of Roslyn and Cle Elum, past the 1883 grist mill at Thorp to the rodeo town of Ellensburg.

members.name: Whidbey Scenic Isle Way
members.blurb: From the Clinton ferry the highway runs the length of Whidbey Island, through Greenbank farmland and the old wharf town of Coupeville on Penn Cove to the high bridge over Deception Pass.
members.note: Shown on the map as Whidbey Island Scenic Byway.

members.name: White Pass Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 12 follows the Cowlitz upstream between the reservoir lakes at Mossyrock, through the timber towns of Morton and Packwood under Mount Rainier, then over White Pass and down to the Naches orchards.

members.name: Yakama Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 97 crosses the Yakama Reservation from the farm plain at Toppenish, a town of murals, up over Satus Pass in the Simcoe Mountains to Goldendale's observatory and the Columbia at Maryhill.

members.name: Yakima River Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR 821 bends with the Yakima River between Ellensburg and Selah under basalt cliffs and golden hills, past BLM river camps where fly fishers and summer floaters put in.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: U.S. 12, Snake River Bridge to Walla Walla
members.blurb: A stretch of the Lewis and Clark Trail on US 12, leaving the Columbia at Wallula and running east past Touchet into Walla Walla, a town of more than a hundred wineries.

members.name: International Selkirk Loop
members.blurb: A loop around the Selkirk Mountains through two countries; in Washington it follows the Pend Oreille River north from Newport past the Kalispel bison herd and Tiger to the border above Metaline Falls.

members.name: Mountain Loop Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A miners' road of 1891 from Granite Falls past the CCC ranger buildings at Verlot, along the South Fork Stillaguamish to Barlow Pass, then fourteen miles of one-lane gravel on the way to Darrington.
